barriers.description: Budget and time constraints forced the team to prioritize a minimal set of interactive features and leave additional features as static backlog illustrations.
barriers.justification: This resource constraint limited the designers' ability to produce full interactive design solutions and to iterate on and integrate additional feature concepts into the working prototype.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Given our budget and time constraints, we prioritized a set of minimal features for our interactive timeline prototype and rendered the backlog content as supplemental static illustrations of additional feature designs.

barriers.description: The evaluation was limited by remote, unsupervised testing with a small number of participants and weak statistical power.
barriers.justification: These limitations constrained the team's ability to robustly evaluate the prototype with users, reducing confidence in testing results and hindering effective integration of feedback and iteration based on representative user data.
barriers.reference_excerpt: There are limitations to this design project. Evaluation of this timeline was completed using expert reviews from a group of clinicians (physicians, nurses, pharmacists), human factors researchers, usability practitioners, and volunteers from the EHR vendor community. Our pilot study was performed unsupervised, remotely, and had a small number of participants with weak statistical power.

barriers.description: Inconsistent and limited prescription, dispense, and adherence data exchange across EHR and pharmacy systems, plus transformations into unstructured text, impeded creation of a precise timeline display.
barriers.justification: These external data and interoperability problems prevented designers from reliably understanding the real data context of use and from specifying and producing accurate timeline representations and evaluating them with authentic data.
barriers.reference_excerpt: We learned from implementation efforts at 1 EHR vendor and 1 client organization that there is inconsistent and limited prescription dispense and adherence data being exchanged or available currently. The transmission of e-prescription details is inconsistent across commercial EHR and pharmacy software products, thus limiting the consistent display of prescription instruction detail. When the data are exchanged from EHR to e-prescribing hub to pharmacy software, or make the return trip for a renewal request, the data may undergo transformation that introduces new ambiguity.
